choice.sequential_rereads: CHOSEN (the idea). certify/20s: a random-walk (SPRT) stopping rule per bit instead of certify/20n's fixed odd k. Bit j of observation t is re-read until its lead |#ones - #zeros| first reaches m_t, the smallest m with read_bits * r^m/(1+r^m) <= delta*6/(pi^2 t^2), r = eps_bar/(1-eps_bar). Gambler's ruin gives the per-bit error exactly (r_eps^m/(1+r_eps^m), monotone in eps), so the anytime guarantee is the same delta as certify/20n's but the read count is about m/(1-2 eps) per observation instead of log(.)/(2(1/2-eps_bar)^2). Pre-data calculation (no worlds, no seeds; 2000 simulated walks per row, 2 bits, delta 0.001): at eps 0.10/eps_bar 0.15 and t = 150 the fixed rule needs 75 reads, the sequential rule about 15; at eps 0.20/0.25, 145 vs about 32; at eps 0.30/0.35 the fixed rule needs about 400.
choice.inner_solver: frozen certify/20p (clique-anchored), declared N 20, 2-bit readings, scale20 worlds; the inner solver is unchanged, so every settled-correct noisy trace equals the noise-free trace and the noisy record must equal the noise-free record (gate GEQ65). Noise is absorbed entirely in the front end.
choice.how_far: three noise levels, eps 0.10, 0.20 and 0.30 (eps_bar 0.15, 0.25, 0.35); 0.30 at 2 bits is the stretch and the gated headline

rejected.fixed-k majority (certify/20n rule) as a: under correct majorities its inner trace equals the noise-free trace, so its decisions equal C20's exactly; only its read count differs and that is a deterministic function of the observation count (Exact). Reported as a counterfactual from certify20n.reads_for on each record's observation count, not run (saves about 20 min of duplicate SAT work)
rejected.noise at 24 states: P24 decided 2/6 noise-free in study-064; noise cannot add decisions, so 20 states is where noise can be measured; 24-32 states with noise is a later version

honest_framing: The SAT side is unchanged, so this version cannot decide more worlds than noise-free certify/20p; the claim under test is that sequential re-reads remove the noise penalty at far lower read cost, up to eps 0.30 at 2 bits, with the same delta guarantee. A pass extends a certification to noisy 2-bit 20-state worlds; a fail (any settled-bit error, a record mismatch with C20, or reads not below 0.35x of the fixed rule) is published plainly.

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify20s.py (brute.certify/20s), host-agnostic: Certifier20S wraps an unchanged Certifier20P; threshold(t, eps_bar, delta, read_bits), settle(readings, m, read_bits), more(readings), observe(action, readings) where readings must be exactly a stopping sequence; READ_CAP 100000 readings per observation (ValueError beyond). certify/20p, certify/20n and every earlier module are frozen and imported only.
design.worlds: experiments/worlds_065.py: world = worlds_064.world(seed, 'scale20') (2-bit, noise-free emissions, the 063/064 family), passive prefix worlds_026.actions(seed, 0, k). Noise: every bit of every reading is flipped independently with probability eps, drawn from random.Random(seed*13+650+int(round(1000*eps))) in the fixed order (t, read, bit), one random() per bit, flip iff draw < eps; readings are drawn one at a time until certify/20s.more() is False. Re-reads do not move the hidden state.
